literal: When the next day he did not improve, his decline grew severe and lingering; then he was brought into the Green Rush Hall to receive the mandate at the jade armrest.
idiomatic: The next day he grew no better; as his decline deepened he was brought into the Green Rush Hall to receive the mandate at the jade armrest.

literal: When mourning garments were displayed in the court, before the testament could be reached he ascended; he truly received the great treasure, and that very day took the throne.
idiomatic: Mourning garments were already displayed in the court; before the testament could be read he had ascended—he received the great treasure and that very day took the throne.

literal: We therefore are fearful and ashamed; our heart finds no peace.
idiomatic: We are seized with fear and shame; our heart cannot find rest.

literal: Now though we have lost a ruler we have a ruler; the ancestral temple alone is secure. It is fitting to exalt and reward ministers, reaching to the hundred officials—all those in office shall together receive promotion.
idiomatic: Though we have lost a ruler, we have a ruler still; the ancestral temple stands secure. Ministers and the hundred officials alike—all who hold office—should be raised and rewarded.

literal: Civil and military officials within and without, supervising generals and campaign troops who were dismissed from office because of the crisis—all shall receive two grades of military merit;
idiomatic: Civil and military officials at court and in the provinces, supervising generals, and troops on campaign who were dismissed during the crisis shall all receive two grades of military merit;

literal: for palace-guard military officers from Guardian of the Gate downward and personal attendants from Companion upward, and for commanders, three grades of military merit may be granted;
idiomatic: palace-guard officers from Guardian of the Gate down and personal attendants from Companion up, together with field commanders, may receive three grades;

literal: those who lost office or rank may have their titles restored.
idiomatic: those who lost office or rank may have their titles restored.

literal: Those stripped for treason or great rebellion are not within this scope.
idiomatic: Those stripped for treason or great rebellion are excluded.

literal: Pure-critique bans and prohibitions are also entirely remitted.
idiomatic: Pure-critique bans and prohibitions are also entirely lifted.

literal: If those of second rank and above cannot accept the grant themselves, they may confer it on younger brothers.
idiomatic: If holders of second rank and above cannot accept the grant themselves, they may pass it to a younger brother.

literal: Proclaim far and near so that all may know.
idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed far and near so that all may know.

literal: " On yimao, the young lord ascended the throne.
idiomatic: " On yimao the young lord ascended the throne.

literal: Equal in Three Departments and Grand Commander Erzhu Rong submitted a memorial asking to enter and hurry to the capital; he mustered troops and marched south.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, equal in rank to the Three Departments and grand commander, submitted a memorial asking leave to march to the capital; he mustered his army and turned south.

literal: That month Du Luozhou was absorbed by Ge Rong.
idiomatic: That month Du Luozhou was absorbed by Ge Rong.

literal: Third month, guimao day: Ge Rong captured Cangzhou, seized Inspector Xue Qingzhi; eight or nine tenths of the inhabitants died.
idiomatic: In the third month, on the guimao day, Ge Rong took Cangzhou and seized Inspector Xue Qingzhi; eight or nine residents in ten perished.

literal: On jiashen the elevated posthumous title was Emperor Xiaoming; on yiyou he was buried at Ding Mausoleum; temple name Suzong.
idiomatic: On jiashen the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming was elevated; on yiyou he was buried at Ding Mausoleum with temple name Suzong.

literal: Summer, fourth month, xuxu day: Erzhu Rong crossed the river.
idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the xuxu day, Erzhu Rong crossed the Yellow River.

literal: On gengzi the Empress Dowager and the young lord died.
idiomatic: On gengzi the Empress Dowager and the young lord died.

literal: The historian says: From Emperor Xuanwu onward in Wei, the governing net was not drawn taut.
idiomatic: The historian writes: From Emperor Xuanwu onward the Wei court no longer held the reins of government.

literal: Suzong at tender age inherited the enterprise; Empress Linghou as a woman held sole power, entrusted office to unworthy men, and rewards and punishments went awry.
idiomatic: Suzong came to the throne in childhood; Empress Linghou ruled as a woman alone, entrusted power to the wrong men, and rewards and punishments lost all measure.

literal: Then trouble rose on four sides, calamity spread to the capital region, and in the end his reign was not long.
idiomatic: Trouble rose on every side; disaster reached the capital; in the end his reign was brief.

literal: This too was the beginning of ruin and loss—alas!
idiomatic: This was the beginning of the kingdom's slide into ruin—alas!
